item.title: Solid Agreements
item.description:
Set Expectations

3 Things: Inclusions, Exclusions and Clarifications. This foundation outlines exactly what will be done and how it will be done.

The Importance of Clarity

A well-defined agreement eliminates misunderstandings between the homeowner and the painting contractor. This approach helps everyone know what to expect in terms of scope, cost, and timeline. When all parties understand the plan, there’s far less chance of mismatched expectations or unpleasant surprises.

item.title: Lead Paint: It's Important
item.description:
THE RRP Rule

For homes built before 1978, lead paint may be a factor in how painting work is done. To see that both homeowners and contractors are protected, EPA-accredited training and certification is required of all contractors working on older homes.

The RRP rule (Renovation, Repair and Painting) has been in place since 2011, regular refresher courses are required to maintain certification.

item.title: Touch-ups - Possible?
item.description:
If you’ve ever wondered why a fresh dab of paint doesn’t blend, you’re not alone. Even small touch-ups can be deceptively tricky.

Not as Easy as You Think

Touch-ups appear simple but often lead to unexpected complications in sheen, color, and blending.

The Illusion of “Quick Fixes”

Homeowners often assume a dab of paint will make chips and scuffs disappear. Once dried, slight differences in texture or gloss can actually highlight the touch-up spot instead of hiding it.

item.title: Nail Pops: What To Know
item.description:
nail pop (noun) | ˈnāl ˌpäp| A condition in which a nail protrudes above the surface of drywall or siding due to structural movement, wood shrinkage, or improper installation.

Nail Pops: What They Are and How to Fix Them

A nail pop is simply a nail head that has pushed above the surface of a wall or siding. These can appear both inside and outside your home, usually due to structural settling, seasonal expansion and contraction, or construction shortcuts. While nail pops can be unsightly, they’re rarely a sign of water intrusion or structural failure. Here’s what you need to know about fixing them the right way.

item.title: Proper Paint Storage - 3 Steps
item.description:
As a general rule of thumb, if a can of paint is less than one third full it is not worth storing - leave the lid off and let it dry completely. Then, leave it out with your household trash - dry paint is considered disposable household trash.

Why Paint Storage Matters

Leftover paint can be a problem or a solution—depending on how you store it.

Most homes have a few partially used cans of paint sitting in a corner or shelf. Whether you’re planning to touch up trim or repaint a whole room, proper storage can mean the difference between usable paint and a hazardous mess.

item.title: Painting Cedar Shake Shingles
item.description:
Cedar shake shingles can split and curl when not properly cared for. While replacing damaged shingles sounds straightforward, here's what to look out for.

Why Painting Shake Shingles Is Tricky

Cedar shakes offer beautiful texture and depth—but they come with quirks that can’t be ignored.

Shakes look great when freshly painted—but the path to that polished finish isn’t always simple. Aging shingles, varied textures, and hidden staining can complicate the process.

item.title: How Much Does Exterior Painting Cost?
item.description:
After deciding to paint, the next question is always cost—and the answer is usually “it depends.”

How Much Does Exterior Painting Cost in Kansas City?

Prices vary widely depending on the home’s size, condition, and architectural complexity.

Smaller Homes vs. Larger Projects

Crestwood Painting has painted cozy ranch homes for as little as $4500. At the other end of the spectrum, we’ve worked on Ward Parkway historic gems that can reach $35,000.

item.title: Top 4 Questions Before a Painting Estimate
item.description:
There are four questions that tell you more about a potential contractor—and the job you’ll actually get.

Don’t Start With “How Much?”

Most homeowners start with: “Can I get an estimate?” That’s a fair question—but it’s not the most important one. Before you even talk about price, it helps to understand who you’re dealing with.

item.title: Choose the Right Paint Sheen
item.description:
When considering how to choose paint sheen, it’s essential to recognize that sheen is as important as color, influencing both appearance and practicality.

Light Reflectance & Sheen

Paint sheen refers to the level of light a surface bounces back into a space. You might wonder, is paint sheen important? Absolutely—higher sheens, like gloss and semi-gloss, reflect more light for a bright, polished look, while flatter sheens absorb light to create a softer effect. This interplay of shine and absorption significantly shapes a room’s ambiance or a home’s exterior impression.

item.title: How to Dispose of Old Paint
item.description:
Properly dealing with leftover paint not only keeps your home clutter-free but also safeguards the environment from hazardous chemicals. Whether you’ve just finished an interior project or wrapped up some exterior touch-up, understanding how to safely handle old paint is important.

The Leftover Paint Dilemma

Storing old paint in basements or garages might seem harmless, but eventually those cans pile up. Disposing of them carelessly can lead to legal and environmental problems. If you still have paint questions, take a look at our FAQs here for additional insights.
